content.comment_body: Hello, I have set up an OpenVPN connection and am able to connect to both master and slave [product_name] devices using [product_name] software. Data exchange between the two devices works during simulation, but fails when connecting over VPN. Does anyone know what could be causing this issue? Thanks.
Hi, I recommend researching "how does port forwarding work" online. Reading about this topic might help clarify what you need.
Thank you. But I am unsure why port forwarding would be necessary when a VPN connection has already been established.

Based on your description, it seems the [version_no] feature for the devices may not be enabled. Without this, establishing a connection is not possible. Also, these devices tend to generate a lot of traffic via [version_no] connections. If you want to connect devices outside of your local network, using Modbus could be more efficient and save data volume, provided you configure the settings correctly.

Hello, as far as I know, these devices need to be on the same subnet. It appears your devices are not. My setup works over WiFi with all devices on the same subnet. Make sure your VPN is configured to provide the same subnet range to your devices.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced a data exchange issue between two [product_name] devices over an OpenVPN connection, although the setup worked in simulation using [product_name] software. The discussion highlighted key networking points such as the need for port forwarding, subnet alignment, and activation of required communication protocols. There was confusion about the necessity of port forwarding with VPN, and advice was given to prefer Modbus communication outside the local network to optimize data usage. Challenges are related to network communication requirements and avoiding configuration mistakes when connecting devices over VPN.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants seamless data exchange between [product_name] devices over VPN, replicating simulation success. They expect this to work without the need for complex network adjustments like port forwarding or subnet configuration.
